full_judgment:
Md Anwarul Haque J: Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 19327 of 2008 and the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No: 19328 of 2008 filed by one Moulana Motiur Rahman Nizami, accused of. ACC GR Case No. 22 of 2008 arising out of Shahbagh PS Case No. 53 dated 26-2-2008 punishable under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 pending before the Special Court No. 2, Dhaka and one Ali Ahsan Md. Mozahidn accused of the above mentioned case are taken together for analogous hearing which have been sent by the Hon'ble Appellate Division for hearing by order passed in Criminal petition for leave to Appeal No. 19 of -2009 and 18 of 2009 respectively. In pursuance of such direction we have fixed these two matters for hearing analogously since the question of facts and law involved in these two matters are identical which arises out of same occurrence and the conducting advocates are also the same. It is also decided to hear and dispose of these two matters, referred to above, in one judgment which will go to regulate these petitions respectively. 

 29. Now relating to absence of mens rea as argued by the learned Advocates for petitioner enabling the Court to quash the proceeding we are of the view that in the true nature of things it is not always possible to prove dishonest intention without the help of any evidence, oral or circumstantial. It can only be proved by number of circumstances for which a reasonable inference can be drawn. There is no doubt that mens rea or criminal intention is mental act of the accused persons which is required to be unearthed either by circumstantial or oral evidence to be adduced by the prosecution during the course of trial. Moreover, abusing their position as public servant the accused-petitioners contributed much for obtaining pecuniary benefit for some other person causing loss of more than Taka 150 crores of the government which is enough to constitute the prima-facie element of mens rea as is now required. In this forum created under section 561A interference on such count is neither desirable nor acceptable because this will go to frustrate the legislative intent to secure trial of the accused-persons against whom prima-facie case is found to have been made out. 

 36. In the result, these two rules issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 19327 of 2008 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 19328 of 2008 are discharged.
